claim: Intracellular Ca2+ oscillations occurred in endothelial cells exhibiting angiogenic behavior during sprouting angiogenesis in zebrafish.
source: Here, we visualized endothelial Ca2+ dynamics in zebrafish and found that intracellular Ca2+ oscillations occurred in ECs exhibiting angiogenic behavior.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from in vivo Ca2+ imaging in zebrafish embryos showing oscillations in budding tip cells (Figure 1A,B).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in endothelial cells budding from the dorsal aorta depended upon VEGF receptor-2 (Vegfr2).
source: Ca2+ oscillations depended upon VEGF receptor-2 (Vegfr2) and Vegfr3 in ECs budding from the dorsal aorta (DA) and posterior cardinal vein, respectively.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that ki8751 treatment (Vegfr inhibitor) and vegfr2 morpholino knockdown abolished Ca2+ oscillations in budding tip cells from the DA (Figure 2A-F).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in endothelial cells budding from the posterior cardinal vein depended upon Vegfr3.
source: Ca2+ oscillations depended upon VEGF receptor-2 (Vegfr2) and Vegfr3 in ECs budding from the dorsal aorta (DA) and posterior cardinal vein, respectively.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that vegfr3 morphants lost Ca2+ oscillations in venous sprouts from the PCV (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–D).

claim: Visualizing Ca2+ oscillations allowed monitoring of endothelial cell responses to angiogenic cues.
source: Thus, visualizing Ca2+ oscillations allowed us to monitor EC responses to angiogenic cues.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Ca2+ oscillations depend on VEGFR signaling and occur in cells exhibiting angiogenic behavior.

claim: Vegfr-dependent Ca2+ oscillations occurred in migrating tip cells as well as stalk cells budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: Vegfr-dependent Ca2+ oscillations occurred in migrating tip cells as well as stalk cells budding from the DA.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations in both tip and stalk cells during budding, which were abolished by ki8751 treatment (Figure 5A-C).

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling was required for the selection of single stalk cell as well as tip cell.
source: We investigated how Dll4/Notch signaling regulates endothelial Ca2+ oscillations and found that it was required for the selection of single stalk cell as well as tip cell.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that dll4 morphants had increased numbers of Ca2+-oscillating cells during both tip cell and stalk cell budding (Figure 9A, Figure 10A-D).

claim: GCaMP7a is an improved version of GCaMP that increases fluorescence upon Ca2+ elevation.
source: GCaMP7a is an improved version of GCaMP (Nakai et al., 2001), an engineered GFP that increases fluorescence upon the Ca2+ elevation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Nakai et al., 2001) and experimental validation showing fluorescence increase with ionomycin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).

claim: Budding tip cells from the dorsal aorta showed sustained and non-periodic Ca2+ oscillations at 24-27 somite stages.
source: These tip cells showed sustained and non-periodic Ca2+ oscillations (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C and Video 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from time-lapse imaging showing oscillatory Ca2+ dynamics in budding tip cells (Figure 1A,B).

claim: The time to reach the peak of individual Ca2+ oscillations in tip cells varied from 5.6 to 18.7 seconds with an average of 9.0 seconds.
source: The time to reach the peak of individual oscillations was varied 5.6–18.7 s (average, 9.0 s) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of time-lapse 2D imaging data (Figure 1C).

claim: Repetitive Ca2+ transients were not detected in other endothelial cells within the dorsal aorta during tip cell budding.
source: Repetitive Ca2+ transients were not detected in other ECs within the DA (Figure 1A,B,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations only in budding tip cells and not in other DA cells (Figure 1A,B,D).

claim: Treatment with ki8751 completely abolished Ca2+ oscillations in budding tip cells from the dorsal aorta.
source: When we treated 22 ss embryos with ki8751 and performed Ca2+ imaging analyses at 24–27 ss, the Ca2+ oscillations detected in budding tip cells of control embryos (Figure 1) were completely abolished by the treatment of ki8751 (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing Ca2+ oscillations in control versus ki8751-treated embryos (Figure 2A-C).

claim: ki8751 treatment stopped tip cell migration from the dorsal aorta.
source: Tip cell migration stopped in ki8751-treated embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), confirming that ki8751 inhibits Vegfr2 of zebrafish.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing blocked tip cell migration in ki8751-treated embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claim: ki8751 might also inhibit Vegfr3 activity in zebrafish.
source: ki8751 might also inhibit Vegfr3 activity, because, in our previous results, ki8751 treatment blocked Vegfr3-dependent venous sprout from the PCV in zebrafish (Kwon et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work showing ki8751 blocks Vegfr3-dependent venous sprouting (Kwon et al., 2013).

claim: Knockdown of vegfr2 markedly reduced Ca2+ oscillations in budding cells from the dorsal aorta.
source: Although we observed partial sprouts from the DA in the morphants as reported in vegfr2 mutants (Covassin et al., 2006), Ca2+ oscillations were markedly reduced in these budding cells (Figure 2D–F), suggesting that Ca2+ oscillations in ECs budding from the DA are dependent upon Vegfr2 activation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing reduced Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr2 morphants (Figure 2D-F) and citation to previous work on vegfr2 mutants (Covassin et al., 2006).

claim: Co-expression of sFlt1 and NLS-mC in endothelial cells completely inhibited Ca2+ oscillations of cells close to somite boundaries.
source: While expression of control NLS-tagged mCherry (NLS-mC) did not affect Ca2+ oscillations in budding ECs (Figure 2G–I; NLS-mC), co-expression of sFlt1 and NLS-mC in ECs completely inhibited Ca2+ oscillations of ECs close to somite boundaries (Figure 2G–I; sFlt1+NLS-mC).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing Ca2+ oscillations in cells expressing NLS-mC alone versus sFlt1+NLS-mC (Figure 2G-I).

claim: Tip cell sprouting was inhibited by expressing sFlt1.
source: Tip cell sprouting was also inhibited by expressing sFlt1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), as previously reported (Zygmunt et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing inhibited ISV sprouting in sFlt1-expressing regions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and citation to previous work (Zygmunt et al., 2011).

claim: Vegfa/Vegfr2 signaling is required for Ca2+ oscillations during tip cell budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: Collectively, our results indicate that Vegfa/Vegfr2 signaling is required for the Ca2+ oscillations during tip cell budding from the DA.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing that inhibition of Vegfr2 (by ki8751, vegfr2 MO, or sFlt1) abolishes Ca2+ oscillations in budding tip cells.

claim: vegfr3 morphants exhibited loss of venous sprout from the posterior cardinal vein.
source: vegfr3 morphants exhibited loss of venous sprout from the PCV (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and phenocopied vegfr3 null mutant fish (Hogan et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing loss of venous sprouts in vegfr3 morphants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) and citation to previous work on vegfr3 mutants (Hogan et al., 2009).

claim: vegfr3 morphants did not show any alteration of Ca2+ oscillations during tip cell budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: These vegfr3 morphants did not show any alteration of Ca2+ oscillations during tip cell budding (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing normal Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr3 morphants during arterial sprouting (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C).

claim: Vegfr3 is not involved in Ca2+ responses during vessel sprouting from the dorsal aorta.
source: These results suggest that Vegfr3 is not involved in the Ca2+ responses during vessel sprouting from the DA.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing no change in Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr3 morphants during arterial sprouting.

claim: Tip cells in venous sprouts from the posterior cardinal vein exhibited Ca2+ oscillations in a manner dependent upon Vegfr3.
source: We observed that tip cells in the venous sprouts from the PCV exhibited Ca2+ oscillations in a manner dependent upon Vegfr3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations in venous sprouts that were lost in vegfr3 morphants (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-D).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations occur in both arterial and venous sprouting.
source: Thus, Ca2+ oscillations are not only specific for arterial sprouting, but also occur in venous sprouting that is regulated by Vegfc/Vegfr3 signaling.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations of Ca2+ oscillations in both arterial (Vegfr2-dependent) and venous (Vegfr3-dependent) sprouting.

claim: Prior to sprouting from the dorsal aorta, Ca2+ oscillations occurred widely within the dorsal aorta.
source: Prior to sprouting from the DA, Ca2+ oscillations occurred widely within the DA (Figure 3A,B and Video 2) and were completely dependent upon Vegfr2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations throughout the DA before sprouting (Figure 3A,B) and their dependence on Vegfr2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D).

claim: Ca2+-oscillating cells were not restricted to specific regions within the dorsal aorta before vessel sprouting.
source: Although ISV sprouts usually emerge from the DA just anterior to each somite boundary (Zygmunt et al., 2011), Ca2+-oscillating cells were not restricted to specific regions within the DA before vessel sprouting (17–19 ss, Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing similar Ca2+ oscillation frequency and mean ΔF/F0 across different regions of the DA (Figure 3C) and citation to previous work on ISV emergence (Zygmunt et al., 2011).

claim: Single tip cells are not specified among endothelial cells of the dorsal aorta before sprouting as far as Ca2+ oscillation is used as an indicator.
source: These results suggest that single tip cells are not specified among the ECs of the DA before sprouting as far as Ca2+ oscillation is used as an indicator (Figure 3D).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Ca2+ oscillations occur broadly in the DA before sprouting without spatial restriction.

claim: Loss of Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr2 morphants was rescued in endothelial cells expressing Vegfr2.
source: Loss of Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr2 morphants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D) was rescued in ECs expressing Vegfr2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F), indicating a specific role of Vegfr2 in Ca2+ oscillations.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing rescue of Ca2+ oscillations in vegfr2 morphants by Vegfr2 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).

claim: When endothelial cells within the dorsal aorta started to sprout dorsally, Ca2+ oscillations were detected in two neighboring cells in 45.2% or single cells in 52.4% at somite boundaries.
source: When ECs within the DA started to sprout dorsally (19–22 ss), Ca2+ oscillations were detected in two neighboring ECs (45.2%) or single ECs (52.4%) at somite boundaries, either of which sprouted dorsally (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of the number of Ca2+-oscillating cells at somite boundaries during early sprouting (Figure 4A).

claim: The initial selection of single tip cells is not completed just after the onset of vessel sprouting.
source: These results suggest that the initial selection of single tip cells is not completed just after the onset of vessel sprouting.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that two neighboring cells can exhibit Ca2+ oscillations at the onset of sprouting.

claim: Ca2+ response became restricted to single tip cells at 24-27 somite stages.
source: Ca2+ response became restricted to single tip cells at later stage (24–27 ss) (Figure 4A), suggesting the completion of tip cell selection.
evidence: Supported by quantitative data showing that at 24-27 ss, 90.9% of somite boundaries had single Ca2+-oscillating cells (Figure 4A).

claim: During tip cell selection between two neighboring cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations, only one cell maintained the oscillations over time.
source: Then, to visualize the process of tip cell selection between two neighboring cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations, we performed Ca2+ imaging for a longer period and found that only one cell maintained the oscillations over time (Figure 4B,C and Video 3).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data showing one cell maintaining Ca2+ oscillations while the other loses them (Figure 4B,C).

claim: Endothelial cells losing Ca2+ response retracted their sprout.
source: We also noticed that the ECs losing Ca2+ response retracted their sprout (Figure 4B), implying that these cells lost their ability to respond to angiogenic cues.
evidence: Supported by observational data from time-lapse imaging showing sprout retraction in cells losing Ca2+ oscillations (Figure 4B).

claim: Endothelial cells showing sustained Ca2+ oscillations eventually became tip cells.
source: The ECs showing sustained Ca2+ oscillations eventually became tip cells (18/18, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative tracking data showing all cells with sustained Ca2+ oscillations became tip cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claim: The initial selection of tip cells is determined even after endothelial cells start to migrate from the dorsal aorta.
source: Thus, our results provide evidence that the initial selection of tip cells is determined even after ECs start to migrate from the DA (Figure 4D).
evidence: Inferred from observations showing tip cell selection occurring after the onset of sprouting.

claim: plxnD1 morphants displayed ectopic endothelial cell sprouts that exhibited Ca2+ oscillations.
source: We observed ectopically budding ECs exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations in plxnD1 morphants (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), confirming an essential role of PlxnD1 in the allocation of budding ECs from the DA.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing ectopic Ca2+-oscillating sprouts in plxnD1 morphants (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).

claim: PlexinD1 is essential for determining the position of tip cell budding in the vicinity of somite boundaries.
source: Sema-PlexinD1 (PlxnD1) signaling is required to determine the position of tip cell budding in the vicinity of somite boundaries (Zygmunt et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Zygmunt et al., 2011) and confirmed by experimental data showing ectopic budding in plxnD1 morphants.

claim: Sustained repetitive Ca2+ oscillations occurred in tip cells when endothelial cells following tip cells were budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: We then examined Ca2+ dynamics at later stages of ISV formation. Sustained repetitive Ca2+ oscillations in tip cells were observed when ECs following tip cells were budding from the DA (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations in tip cells during stalk cell budding (Figure 5A-C).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations occurred in budding stalk cells.
source: Interestingly, Ca2+ oscillations also occurred in budding stalk cells (Figure 5A,B and Video 4), although their oscillation frequency and mean ΔF/F0 were lower than those in tip cells (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells with lower frequency and amplitude than tip cells (Figure 5A-D).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in both tip cells and budding stalk cells were Vegfr-dependent.
source: We further found that the Ca2+ oscillations both in tip cells and budding stalk cells were Vegfr-dependent (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that ki8751 treatment abolished Ca2+ oscillations in both tip and stalk cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations were not detected in endothelial cells that remained in the dorsal aorta during stalk cell budding.
source: In clear contrast, we did not detect Ca2+ oscillations in other ECs that remained in the DA (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing absence of Ca2+ oscillations in DA cells during stalk cell budding (Figure 5A-C).

claim: Stalk cells that are budding from the dorsal aorta have significant Vegfr2 activity, albeit weaker than that in tip cells.
source: Stalk cells that are budding from the DA have significant Vegfr2 activity, albeit weaker than that in tip cells.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that stalk cells exhibit Ca2+ oscillations (which depend on Vegfr2) but with lower frequency and amplitude than tip cells (Figure 5D).

claim: Endothelial cells expressing dominant-negative Vegfr2 rarely became tip and stalk cells and remained in the dorsal aorta.
source: While expression of NLS-mC alone neither affect tip, stalk, nor DA cells (Figure 6C,D; NLS-mC), the cells expressing both Vegfr2-ΔC and NLS-mC rarely became tip and stalk cells and remained in the DA (Figure 6C,D; Vegfr2-ΔC+NLS-mC).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that Vegfr2-ΔC-expressing cells predominantly remained in the DA rather than becoming tip or stalk cells (Figure 6C,D).

claim: Activation of Vegfr2 in tip cells and stalk cells is crucial for their exit from the dorsal aorta.
source: These results suggest that the activation of Vegfr2 in tip cells and stalk cells is crucial for their exit from the DA.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing that cells expressing dominant-negative Vegfr2 fail to exit the DA.

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells out of the dorsal aorta were comparable to those in tip cells.
source: We then investigated Ca2+ dynamics after stalk cells completely came out from the DA. Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells out of the DA were comparable to those in tip cells (Figure 7A–C and Video 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing similar Ca2+ oscillation frequency and mean ΔF/F0 in tip and stalk cells after stalk cells exited the DA (Figure 7A-C).

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells after exiting the dorsal aorta were dependent upon Vegfr2.
source: The Ca2+ oscillations were also dependent upon Vegfr2 (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that ki8751 treatment abolished Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells after they exited the DA (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).

claim: 78.9% of Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells occurred independently of tip cells.
source: We found that 78.9% of Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells occurred independently of tip cells, and 91.6% of oscillations in tip cells occurred independently of stalk cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of synchrony between Ca2+ oscillations in tip and stalk cells (Figure 7D).

claim: 91.6% of Ca2+ oscillations in tip cells occurred independently of stalk cells.
source: We found that 78.9% of Ca2+ oscillations in stalk cells occurred independently of tip cells, and 91.6% of oscillations in tip cells occurred independently of stalk cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of synchrony between Ca2+ oscillations in tip and stalk cells (Figure 7D).

claim: Most Ca2+ oscillations observed in tip and stalk cells occur independently of each other and not through intercellular Ca2+ waves.
source: These results clearly indicate that most Ca2+ oscillations observed in tip and stalk cells occurs independently of each other and not through ICWs.
evidence: Inferred from the quantitative analysis showing that the majority of Ca2+ oscillations in tip and stalk cells are asynchronous.

claim: Not only tip cells but also stalk cells have potential to respond to angiogenic cues.
source: Therefore, our findings suggest that not only tip cells but also stalk cells have potential to respond to angiogenic cues (Figure 7E).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that stalk cells exhibit independent Ca2+ oscillations comparable to tip cells after exiting the DA.

claim: Before sprouting of intersomitic vessels, the number of Ca2+-oscillating endothelial cells and their oscillatory activity were significantly increased in the entire dorsal aorta in dll4 morphants.
source: Before sprouting of ISVs, the number of Ca2+-oscillating ECs and their oscillatory activity were significantly increased in the entire DA in dll4 morphants (Figure 8A–C), suggesting that Dll4 suppresses the Vegfr2-dependent angiogenic responses in entire ECs of the DA.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased Ca2+ oscillation frequency and mean ΔF/F0 across all regions of the DA in dll4 morphants (Figure 8A-C).

claim: Dll4 suppresses Vegfr2-dependent angiogenic responses in entire endothelial cells of the dorsal aorta before sprouting.
source: Before sprouting of ISVs, the number of Ca2+-oscillating ECs and their oscillatory activity were significantly increased in the entire DA in dll4 morphants (Figure 8A–C), suggesting that Dll4 suppresses the Vegfr2-dependent angiogenic responses in entire ECs of the DA.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that loss of Dll4 increases Ca2+ oscillations throughout the DA before sprouting.

claim: When endothelial cells start budding at 19-22 somite stages, Ca2+ responses were restricted to single cells in 44.5% at somite boundaries in control morphants, whereas those were in 20.8% in dll4 morphants.
source: When ECs start budding at 19–22 ss, the Ca2+ responses were restricted to single ECs in 44.5% at somite boundaries in the control morphants, whereas those were, in 20.8% in dll4 morphants (Figure 9A; 19–22 ss).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of the number of Ca2+-oscillating cells at somite boundaries in control versus dll4 morphants (Figure 9A).

claim: Most dll4 morphants had two or more budding endothelial cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations at 19-22 somite stages.
source: Most dll4 morphants had two or more budding ECs exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations (79.2%; Figure 9A; 19–22 ss).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis showing 79.2% of somite boundaries in dll4 morphants had 2 or more Ca2+-oscillating cells (Figure 9A).

claim: Dll4 restricts the number of endothelial cells showing tip cell behavior when they sprout from pre-existing vessels.
source: Thus, our findings support the hypothesis that Dll4 restricts the number of ECs showing tip cell behavior when they sprout from the pre-existing vessels.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that dll4 morphants have increased numbers of Ca2+-oscillating cells during sprouting.

claim: At 24-27 somite stages, while Ca2+ responses became restricted to single tip cells in control embryos, two or more neighboring endothelial cells exhibited Ca2+ oscillations in 74.1% of dll4 morphants.
source: In the later stages (24–27 ss), while the Ca2+ responses became restricted to single tip cells in the control embryos, two or more neighboring ECs exhibited Ca2+ oscillations in dll4 morphants (74.1%; Figure 9A; 24–27 ss).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis showing 74.1% of somite boundaries in dll4 morphants had 2 or more Ca2+-oscillating cells at 24-27 ss (Figure 9A).

claim: In dll4 morphants, repetitive Ca2+ oscillations were maintained in two neighboring endothelial cells, both of which were budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: Consistently in the dll4 morphants, repetitive Ca2+ oscillations were maintained in the two neighboring ECs, both of which were budding from the DA (Figure 9B,C and Video 6).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data showing sustained Ca2+ oscillations in two neighboring budding cells in dll4 morphants (Figure 9B,C).

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling regulates the selection of single tip cell from two or more endothelial cells showing Ca2+ oscillation.
source: These results suggest that Dll4/Notch signaling regulates the selection of single tip cell from two or more ECs showing Ca2+ oscillation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that loss of Dll4 results in multiple cells maintaining Ca2+ oscillations and budding behavior.

claim: In dll4 morphants, Ca2+ responses were detected exclusively in budding endothelial cells, but not in other cells within the dorsal aorta after tip cell budding.
source: In dll4 morphants, Ca2+ responses were detected exclusively in budding ECs, but not in other ECs within the DA (Figure 9D), suggesting that Dll4 suppresses the tip cell behavior especially in ECs adjacent to budding tip cells, but not in the entire DA after tip cell budding.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Ca2+ oscillations only in budding cells and not in other DA cells in dll4 morphants (Figure 9D).

claim: Dll4 suppresses tip cell behavior especially in endothelial cells adjacent to budding tip cells, but not in the entire dorsal aorta after tip cell budding.
source: In dll4 morphants, Ca2+ responses were detected exclusively in budding ECs, but not in other ECs within the DA (Figure 9D), suggesting that Dll4 suppresses the tip cell behavior especially in ECs adjacent to budding tip cells, but not in the entire DA after tip cell budding.
evidence: Inferred from the spatial pattern of Ca2+ oscillations in dll4 morphants showing oscillations only in budding cells.

claim: Treatment with ki8751 completely abolished Ca2+ oscillations observed in dll4 morphants.
source: Treatment with ki8751 completely abolished the Ca2+ oscillations observed in the dll4 morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 2), suggesting that an increase in the number of oscillating cells in the dll4 morphants reflects an increase in the number of ECs showing either Vegfr2 or Vegfr3 activation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing loss of Ca2+ oscillations in dll4 morphants treated with ki8751 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).

claim: An increase in the number of oscillating cells in dll4 morphants reflects an increase in the number of endothelial cells showing either Vegfr2 or Vegfr3 activation.
source: Treatment with ki8751 completely abolished the Ca2+ oscillations observed in the dll4 morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 2), suggesting that an increase in the number of oscillating cells in the dll4 morphants reflects an increase in the number of ECs showing either Vegfr2 or Vegfr3 activation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that ki8751 (which inhibits both Vegfr2 and Vegfr3) abolishes all Ca2+ oscillations in dll4 morphants.

claim: In vegfr3/dll4 double morphants, Ca2+ oscillations were detected in two or more neighboring cells in 65.8% at somite boundaries at 24-27 somite stages.
source: In vegfr3/dll4 double morphants, Ca2+ oscillations were detected in two or more neighboring cells in 65.8% at somite boundaries (Figure 9—figure supplement 3), although the phenotype in the double morphants was slightly milder than that in the dll4 morphants (74.1%; Figure 9A; 24–27 ss).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of Ca2+-oscillating cells in vegfr3/dll4 double morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 3).

claim: Vegfr3 is partially involved in increases in oscillating cells in the absence of Dll4/Notch signaling.
source: Thus, Vegfr3 is partially involved in increases in oscillating cells in the absence of Dll4/Notch signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that the phenotype in vegfr3/dll4 double morphants is slightly milder than in dll4 morphants alone.

claim: Ectopic Ca2+ oscillations occur even in the absence of vegfr3 after inhibiting Dll4/Notch signaling.
source: On the other hand, these results imply that ectopic Ca2+ oscillations occur even in the absence of vegfr3 after inhibiting Dll4/Notch signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that vegfr3/dll4 double morphants still show increased numbers of Ca2+-oscillating cells compared to controls.

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling might restrict the tip cell number mainly by suppressing Vegfr2 signaling.
source: Considering that the Ca2+ responses in dll4 morphants were completely abolished by ki8751 treatment (Figure 9—figure supplement 2), our findings suggest that Dll4/Notch signaling might restrict the tip cell number mainly by suppressing Vegfr2 signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the observations that (1) ki8751 abolishes all Ca2+ oscillations in dll4 morphants and (2) vegfr3 knockdown only partially rescues the dll4 morphant phenotype.

claim: No increase in the expression of vegfr2 or its paralog kdr was detected in the trunk vessels of dll4 morphants.
source: However, we could detect any increase in the expression of neither vegfr2 nor its paralog kdr in the trunk vessels of dll4 morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 4), suggesting that Dll4/Notch signaling inhibits the Vegfr2 signaling cascade rather than vegfr2 expression.
evidence: Supported by whole-mount in situ hybridization data showing no change in vegfr2 or kdr mRNA expression in dll4 morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 4).

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling inhibits the Vegfr2 signaling cascade rather than vegfr2 expression.
source: However, we could detect any increase in the expression of neither vegfr2 nor its paralog kdr in the trunk vessels of dll4 morphants (Figure 9—figure supplement 4), suggesting that Dll4/Notch signaling inhibits the Vegfr2 signaling cascade rather than vegfr2 expression.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that vegfr2 mRNA levels do not change in dll4 morphants despite increased Vegfr2 activity.

claim: When stalk cells began to migrate from the dorsal aorta, Ca2+ oscillations were mainly detected only in single stalk cells in the dorsal aorta.
source: We further investigated the role of Dll4/Notch signaling in stalk cell selection. Of note, when stalk cells began to migrate from the DA, Ca2+ oscillations were mainly detected only in single stalk cells in the DA, but not in adjacent cells apart from tip cells (Figure 10A).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis showing that in control embryos, 73.9% of ISVs had single Ca2+-oscillating stalk cells during stalk cell budding (Figure 10A).

claim: While Ca2+ oscillations were mostly detected in single stalk cell in control embryos, they were often detected in two or more neighboring endothelial cells following tip cells in dll4 morphants.
source: To test this hypothesis, we examined the effect of knockdown of Dll4 on Ca2+ dynamics during stalk cell budding. While Ca2+ oscillations were mostly detected in single stalk cell in the control embryos, they were often detected in two or more neighboring ECs following tip cells in dll4 morphants (Figure 10A–D).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis showing that in dll4 morphants, only 42.9% of ISVs had single Ca2+-oscillating stalk cells, while 57.1% had 2 or more (Figure 10A).

claim: Both Ca2+-oscillating stalk cells in dll4 morphants eventually came out from the dorsal aorta to form intersomitic vessels.
source: Longer time-lapse imaging confirmed that both Ca2+-oscillating stalk cell in the dll4 morphants eventually came out from the DA to form the ISVs.
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging observations in dll4 morphants.

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling regulates the selection of single stalk cell by restricting angiogenic behavior in endothelial cells adjacent to stalk cells.
source: These results suggest that Dll4/Notch signaling regulates the selection of single stalk cell by restricting angiogenic behavior in the ECs adjacent to the stalk cells.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that loss of Dll4 results in multiple stalk cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations and budding behavior.

claim: Even in the absence of dll4, no significant increases in oscillatory activity were detected in both tip and stalk cells that came out of the dorsal aorta.
source: We then investigated the role of Dll4/Notch signaling after stalk cell budding from the DA. Even in the absence of dll4, we could not detect significant increases in oscillatory activity in both tip and stalk cells that came out of the DA (Figure 11A–C).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis showing no significant difference in Ca2+ oscillation frequency or mean ΔF/F0 in tip and stalk cells after budding between control and dll4 morphants (Figure 11C).

claim: Dll4/Notch signaling does not suppress Ca2+ responses in the initial sprouting from the dorsal aorta to form intersomitic vessels.
source: Thus, Dll4/Notch signaling does not suppress the Ca2+-responses in the initial sprouting from the DA to form ISVs.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that dll4 morphants show no increase in Ca2+ oscillatory activity in tip and stalk cells after they exit the DA.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ oscillations occurred in endothelial cells exhibiting angiogenic behavior such as sprouting and migration.
source: Intracellular Ca2+ oscillations occurred in ECs exhibiting angiogenic behavior, such as sprouting and migration.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations throughout the study showing Ca2+ oscillations in budding and migrating tip and stalk cells.

claim: VEGF-A treatment induces Ca2+ rise in cultured human endothelial cells, although their Ca2+ response is not oscillatory.
source: VEGF-A treatment induces Ca2+ rise in cultured human ECs, although their Ca2+ response is not oscillatory (Brock et al., 1991; Favia et al., 2014; Li et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Brock et al., 1991; Favia et al., 2014; Li et al., 2011).

claim: In vitro, VEGF-A induces Ca2+ rise by the PLCγ-IP3-IP3R pathway.
source: In vitro, VEGF-A induces Ca2+ rise by the PLCγ-IP3-IP3R pathway (Koch and Claesson-Welsh, 2012; Moccia et al., 2012), by store-operated Ca2+ entry involving Orai1 and CRAC channel (Li et al., 2011) and by lysosomal Ca2+ release involving two-pore channel TPC2 (Favia et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Koch and Claesson-Welsh, 2012; Moccia et al., 2012; Li et al., 2011; Favia et al., 2014).

claim: VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling is active in stalk cells and is important for cell proliferation in mouse retina angiogenesis.
source: VEGF-A/VEGFR2 signaling is active in stalk cells and is important for cell proliferation in mouse retina angiogenesis (Gerhardt et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Gerhardt et al., 2003).

claim: Vegfr2 activation in stalk cells is necessary for the selection of stalk cells and their exit from the parental vessels during intersomitic vessel formation.
source: Here, we propose that Vegfr2 activation in stalk cells is also necessary for the selection of stalk cells and their exit from the parental vessels during ISV formation.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing that stalk cells exhibit Vegfr2-dependent Ca2+ oscillations and that cells expressing dominant-negative Vegfr2 fail to become stalk cells.

claim: Tip cells and stalk cells can change their positions in elongating vessel sprouts.
source: Jacobsson et al. report that tip cells and stalk cells change their positions in elongating vessels sprouts (Jakobsson et al., 2010), whereas in the earlier stage, we did not observe interexchange of tip cells and stalk cells, suggesting that their plasticity of tip and stalk depends upon the stage and type of angiogenesis.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Jakobsson et al., 2010) and contrasted with observations from this study.

claim: The plasticity of tip and stalk cells depends upon the stage and type of angiogenesis.
source: Jacobsson et al. report that tip cells and stalk cells change their positions in elongating vessels sprouts (Jakobsson et al., 2010), whereas in the earlier stage, we did not observe interexchange of tip cells and stalk cells, suggesting that their plasticity of tip and stalk depends upon the stage and type of angiogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison between previous reports of tip/stalk cell plasticity and the lack of such plasticity observed in this study during early sprouting.

claim: Dll4/Notch-mediated lateral inhibition leads to suppression of angiogenic responses mainly in endothelial cells within the dorsal aorta adjacent to budding tip or stalk cells to restrict excess budding from the dorsal aorta.
source: Thus, our results suggest that Dll4/Notch-mediated lateral inhibition leads to suppression of angiogenic responses mainly in ECs within the DA adjacent to budding tip or stalk cells to restrict excess budding from the DA (Figure 12).
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations showing that (1) Dll4 suppresses Ca2+ oscillations in the entire DA before sprouting, (2) Dll4 restricts the number of budding cells during tip and stalk cell selection, and (3) Dll4 does not suppress Ca2+ oscillations in tip and stalk cells after they exit the DA.

claim: Blood flow-dependent Ca2+ increases were recently reported in zebrafish embryos.
source: Blood flow-dependent Ca2+ increases were recently reported in zebrafish embryos (Goetz et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Goetz et al., 2014).

claim: Ca2+ imaging analysis will be a useful system for understanding quantitatively how individual endothelial cells are regulated by blood flow in vivo.
source: Our Ca2+ imaging analyses have captured flow-dependent Ca2+ oscillations in various types of vessels (Yokota et al., unpublished data): therefore, Ca2+ imaging analysis will be a useful system for understanding quantitatively how individual ECs are regulated by blood flow in vivo.
evidence: Inferred from the authors' unpublished observations of flow-dependent Ca2+ oscillations.

claim: In vivo Ca2+ imaging in endothelial cells will become a powerful tool to investigate the dynamic behavior of individual endothelial cells in vascular development and homeostasis in future studies.
source: Thus, in vivo Ca2+ imaging in ECs presented here will become a powerful tool to investigate the dynamic behavior of individual ECs in vascular development and homeostasis in the future studies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future utility of the Ca2+ imaging method developed in this study.

claim: Tg(fli1:Gal4FF);(UAS:GCaMP7a) transgenic fish line showed an increase of fluorescence exclusively in endothelial cells in response to Ca2+ elevation.
source: This Tg line showed an increase of fluorescence exclusively in ECs in response to Ca2+ elevation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased GCaMP7a fluorescence in ECs after ionomycin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Almost all endothelial cells expressed GCaMP7a in developing trunk vessels of Tg(fli1:Gal4FF);(UAS:GCaMP7a);(fli1:H2B-mC) embryos.
source: We confirmed that almost all ECs expressed GCaMP7a in developing trunk vessels of these triple Tg embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), although the expression of GCaMP7a varied among ECs.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing widespread GCaMP7a expression in trunk vessel ECs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).

claim: Light sheet microscopy allows rapid acquisitions in living embryos by illuminating the sample with a focused light sheet perpendicularly to the direction of observation.
source: To monitor fast Ca2+ dynamics in ECs (see Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C), we used a light sheet microscopy, which allows rapid acquisitions in living embryos by illuminating the sample with a focused light sheet perpendicularly to the direction of observation (Huisken et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work describing light sheet microscopy (Huisken et al., 2004) and established knowledge about the technique.

claim: In every Ca2+ oscillation, a Ca2+ spike occurs throughout the cytoplasm.
source: In every oscillation, a Ca2+ spike occurs throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse 2D imaging data showing Ca2+ increases throughout the cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).

claim: Frequency of Ca2+ oscillations is elevated by increased levels of agonists in some cases in endothelial cells.
source: Frequency of Ca2+ oscillations is elevated by increased levels of agonists in some cases in ECs (Carter et al., 1991; Jacob et al., 1988; Moccia et al., 2003; Mumtaz et al., 2011) and non-ECs (Woods et al., 1986).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Carter et al., 1991; Jacob et al., 1988; Moccia et al., 2003; Mumtaz et al., 2011; Woods et al., 1986).

claim: The amplitude of Ca2+ rise and total Ca2+ increases may possibly reflect the dose of agonists.
source: Meanwhile, the amplitude of Ca2+ rise and total Ca2+ increases may possibly reflect the dose of agonists (Brock et al., 1991; Fewtrell, 1993; Sage et al., 1989).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Brock et al., 1991; Fewtrell, 1993; Sage et al., 1989).

claim: Enhancement of GCaMP7a fluorescence by VEGF-A is blocked by pretreatment with BAPTA-AM.
source: Note that enhancement of GCaMP7a fluorescence by VEGF-A is blocked by pretreatment with BAPTA-AM.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that BAPTA-AM pretreatment prevents VEGF-A-induced GCaMP7a fluorescence increase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Two neighboring Ca2+-oscillating cells at the onset of sprouting were not the result of a recent division in 86% of cases.
source: We confirmed that two neighboring ECs were not the result of a recent division (86%, n = 7, data not shown).
evidence: Supported by observational data from the authors' experiments.

claim: ISV sprouts emerge bilaterally from the dorsal aorta.
source: Since ISV sprouts emerge bilaterally from the DA, we analyzed one side of sprouting ISVs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish vascular development.

claim: Vegfr2-ΔC can block Vegfaa/Vegfr2 signaling in zebrafish endothelial cells.
source: Firstly, to validate whether Vegfr2-ΔC can block Vegfa/Vegfr2 signaling in zebrafish ECs, we established a Tg fish line, Tg(fli1:Gal4ff);(UAS:Vegfr2-ΔC,NLS-mC), that expresses Vegfr2-ΔC simultaneously with NLS-mC in ECs. In primary culture cells dissociated from the Tg embryos, Vegfaa-induced Erk phosphorylation was blocked in the Vegfr2-ΔC-expressing ECs (Figure 6A,B; Vegfr2-ΔC+NLS-mC).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that Vegfr2-ΔC expression blocks Vegfaa-induced Erk phosphorylation (Figure 6A,B).

claim: ISV sprouting was blocked in transgenic embryos expressing Vegfr2-ΔC in endothelial cells.
source: Consistently, ISV sprouting was blocked in the Tg embryos expressing Vegfr2-ΔC in ECs.
evidence: Supported by observational data from transgenic embryos.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ oscillations generally occur through the concerted action between several Ca2+ transporters.
source: Since intracellular Ca2+ oscillations generally occur through the concerted action between several Ca2+ transporters (Smedler and Uhlen, 2014), further studies are needed to delineate whether Vegfr2 signaling directly regulates Ca2+ store or Ca2+ channels in ECs in vivo.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Smedler and Uhlen, 2014) and established knowledge about Ca2+ signaling mechanisms.

claim: In cultured endothelial cells, polarized Ca2+ oscillations occur only in the front of the cells but not in the rear during migration.
source: In cultured ECs, they exhibit Ca2+ oscillations only in the front of the cells but not in the rear during migration (Tsai et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Tsai et al., 2014).

claim: Lateral inhibitory action of Dll4/Notch signaling is essential for selection of tip cells.
source: Lateral inhibitory action of Dll4/Notch signaling is essential for selection of tip cells (Eilken and Adams, 2010; Lohela et al., 2009; Phng and Gerhardt, 2009); however, it is unknown how stalk cells are specified and migrate from the parental vessels.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Eilken and Adams, 2010; Lohela et al., 2009; Phng and Gerhardt, 2009).

claim: It is unknown how stalk cells are specified and migrate from the parental vessels.
source: Lateral inhibitory action of Dll4/Notch signaling is essential for selection of tip cells (Eilken and Adams, 2010; Lohela et al., 2009; Phng and Gerhardt, 2009); however, it is unknown how stalk cells are specified and migrate from the parental vessels.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: In the earlier stage of sprouting, tip cells and stalk cells do not interchange their positions.
source: Jacobsson et al. report that tip cells and stalk cells change their positions in elongating vessels sprouts (Jakobsson et al., 2010), whereas in the earlier stage, we did not observe interexchange of tip cells and stalk cells, suggesting that their plasticity of tip and stalk depends upon the stage and type of angiogenesis.
evidence: Supported by observational data from this study showing no interchange during early sprouting.

claim: It has not been determined whether tip cells also suppress angiogenic responses in stalk cells via Dll4/Notch signaling during vessel elongation.
source: Meanwhile, it has not been determined whether tip cells also suppress angiogenic responses in stalk cells via Dll4/Notch signaling during vessel elongation.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Inhibitory activity of Dll4 toward Ca2+ responses in stalk cells diminishes after stalk cells come out from the dorsal aorta.
source: Our results indicate that inhibitory activity of Dll4 toward Ca2+ responses in stalk cells diminishes after stalk cells come out from the DA.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing no difference in Ca2+ oscillations between control and dll4 morphants after stalk cells exit the DA.

claim: Endothelial Ca2+ responses can be used as an indicator of cellular responses to extracellular stimuli.
source: Endothelial Ca2+ responses can be used as an indicator of cellular responses to extracellular stimuli.
evidence: Inferred from the study's demonstration that Ca2+ oscillations reflect VEGFR signaling and angiogenic behavior.

claim: Blood flow is a well-studied input that induces an intracellular Ca2+ increase in endothelial cells.
source: Among them, blood flow is a well-studied input that induces an intracellular Ca2+ increase in ECs (Ando and Yamamoto, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Ando and Yamamoto, 2013).
